description:
The '''Venezuelan bambuco''' is a musical genre native to the [[Andean natural region|Colombian Andes]] that became popular in [[Venezuela]] after the colonial period. It is typical of the [[Andean Region, Venezuela|Andean region of Venezuela]] and is also found in the States of [[Zulia]], [[Bolívar (state)|Bolívar]], [[Lara (state)|Lara]], and in the Capital District ([[Caracas]]). The instruments typically used are [[piano]], bass, and [[guitar]], and sometimes mandolin and [[flute]]. Venezuelan bambuco is typically played in a 5/8 meter.

Characteristic pieces include: "Mañanitas Navidenas" by Marco Antonio Useche, "Brisas del Torbes" by [[Luis Felipe Ramón y Rivera]], “Tu Partida” by Augusto Brandt, “Serenata” by Manuel Enrique Perez
Diaz and “Hendrina” by Napoleón Lucena.
